title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase to $4.56 (+5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Two prior weeks at $4.56: sales 195 (x0.94) and 119 (x0.57); median x0.85 vs baseline. Noise-adjusted estimate suggests x0.85. One past price hike, so shrink to x0.85.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. A 5.1% price increase to $4.56 (from $4.34) is notable, but recent data shows price hikes to $4.56 (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) led to 195 and 119 units—down 6.2% and 43.0% vs baseline. The noise-adjusted effect of price increases is negative, with a median drop of x0.85. A heatwave (38°C) may boost demand slightly, but milk is not a heat-driven product; no historical evidence shows uplift. No events or promotions. The classical model suggests no change, but price effect overrides that. Shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence. Downside spread increases due to price uncertainty.

This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
